public_rationale: Marcus forecast that AI agents would work on some prompts some of the time, sometimes give strange results, and be hard to predict. A June 2025 benchmark, tau2-bench, ran leading agents repeatedly on the same tasks. Success fell as more runs had to succeed, showing inconsistent results on identical tasks. Anthropic's 2025 Project Vend documented an agent running a shop that claimed it would deliver goods in person wearing a blazer and tie, then emailed security in confusion. Both are dated, published evidence that meets the early resolution rule. The claim is heavily hedged, so the bar is low, but the evidence clears it.
limitations: The claim is hedged and sets a low bar.
There is no direct measure of whether users can predict outcomes in advance.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: AI agents will behave inconsistently. The same agent on the same task will sometimes succeed and sometimes fail, sometimes with odd outputs, so users cannot easily predict the result.

The forecast has no deadline. Early resolution rule: it is settled as supported if, after the post, a published repeated-trial evaluation shows leading agents succeeding on some runs and failing on others for the same tasks, and documented agent runs show strange, unexpected behaviour. It would be contradicted if agents were shown to behave consistently and predictably across repeated runs.
criteria.support_condition: Post-January-2025 evaluations show success dropping when the same tasks are repeated (pass^k falling below pass^1) and document strange agent behaviour.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Post-January-2025 evaluations show leading agents giving consistent, predictable results across repeated trials of the same tasks, with no notable strange behaviour.

evidence.excerpt: However, as k increases, the pass ^\hat{} k scores decline more rapidly for telecom compared to airline, suggesting less consistent performance on the telecom domain.
evidence.explanation: Repeated trials of the same tasks show a leading agent succeeding on some runs and not others. Success falls as more runs must all succeed, so results on any one run are hard to predict.

evidence.excerpt: Claudius claimed it would deliver products “in person” to customers while wearing a blue blazer and a red tie. Anthropic employees questioned this, noting that, as an LLM, Claudius can’t wear clothes or carry out a physical delivery.
evidence.explanation: An agent running a real shop produced strange, unexpected results that its operators did not anticipate. This matches the forecast of 'strange results'.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: A published post-January-2025 repeated-trial evaluation shows a leading agent's success falling across repeated runs of the same tasks. Together with documented strange behaviour (e2), this meets the stated rule.
